body:
## Ask

Grow the family (today: vibey, vibey-bootstrap, vibey-gh, vibey-skills) with new sibling
repos, each following the established conventions — vibey-gh-managed workflows, pinned
tooling, fingerprint, ProperDocs site, the local-review fallback:

| Repo | Scope |
|---|---|
| **vibey-jira** | Jira as a delivery surface: issues in/out of the six-phase conductor, milestone sync |
| **vibey-social** | Social media updates across platforms (Moltbook integration tracked as vibey-gh#139) |
| **vibey-career** | Resume / career / LinkedIn upkeep, driven by actual shipped work |
| **vibey-opencode** | opencode runner integration, sibling to the existing *loop runners |
| **vibey-aws / vibey-azure / vibey-gcp** | Cloud apps, one repo per provider — suffix convention `-aws`/`-azure`/`-gcp` |
| **vibey-word-of-mouth** | Outreach over email, SMS, and physical post (USPS / UPS / FedEx) |

## The one design principle that applies to every repo above

**Interactive, never broadcast-only.** Nothing in this family just posts. Every surface
that emits (a social post, an email, a Jira comment, a LinkedIn update) must also be able
to *respond* — to people and to bots — with rate limits, identity labelling, and per-repo
opt-in. A poster is a spam cannon; a participant is a teammate. This is the acceptance bar
for each repo, not a nice-to-have.

## Doctrine (binding on every repo in this list)

For engineers, by engineers, forever free. Each of these tools works standalone, for free,
for FOSS use, at full capability — the paid dimension (see the monetization issue) is
tailoring, hosting, and convenience, never capability withheld from the free path. A new
repo that cannot satisfy that does not join the family.

## Sequencing

Not all at once. Propose: vibey-opencode first (nearest to existing runner work), then
vibey-jira (feeds the conductor), then the outreach set once the interaction machinery
exists to share.

Made-With: Vibey, the auto-vibecoding machine by Adam Matthew Steinberger

## Triage — 2026-09-17 (`develop` @ f2467910, v0.8.0)

**Status: NOT STARTED** · size **XL** · confidence high

**The ask, as read:** Add eight new members to the family (jira, social, career, opencode, aws, azure, gcp, word-of-mouth), each following the house conventions and each interactive (able to respond, not just emit), starting with vibey-opencode then vibey-jira.

### What already ships
- Nothing from the issue's table. Adjacent groundwork only: pyproject.toml:78-81 makes the workspace members a glob, so a new member registers itself (ADR-0021/0022), and src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/conversation.py:1-27 implements the issue's 'interactive, never broadcast-only' principle on exactly one surface (GitHub comment threads: opt-in for strangers, bounded interactions per thread, never answers itself). Neither is a repo from the list.
- src/vibey_tools/bootstrap/vibey_bootstrap/email/__init__.py is an Azure Communication Services email sender that vibey-word-of-mouth could build on - unused by anything today.

### Evidence in the tree
- src/vibey_runners/ contains only agy, claude, codex, common, cursor, qwen - no opencode member
- src/vibey_tools/ contains only bootstrap, gh, skills - no jira, social, career, aws, gcp or word-of-mouth member
- src/vibey/domain/engine.py:16-21 EngineId is CLAUDELOOP, CODEXLOOP, CURSORLOOP, AGYLOOP, QWENLOOP - no OPENCODE, so nothing can enter rotation
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/failover.py:84 Seat(name="opencode", launch="opencode") - the only 'opencode' in the tree is a default seat NAME in machine-level operator failover that shells out to whatever binary the operator installs; it is not a runner package, has no adapter, and never touches the conductor's engine pool
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/cli.py:1152-1167 wires that failover command - confirming the opencode reference is operator-seat relief, not engine integration
- grep -rn jira --include='*.py' over the whole tree returns 0 hits
- …and 6 more

### What is actually left
- Create src/vibey_runners/opencode as a workspace member: pyproject.toml, Python floor, own test suite and gates per ADR-0022
- Add EngineId.OPENCODE to src/vibey/domain/engine.py and a full EngineDescriptor (binary, min_version, state_dir, done_marker, capabilities, effort_projection, costs, context_window, supports_cwd_flag, plan_flag)
- Add an opencode EngineAdapter under src/vibey/infrastructure/engines/ and register it in bootstrap.py's EngineSelector so BUILD rotation can pick it
- Run the 9-check conformance sweep (src/vibey/application/conformance.py) against the real opencode binary before it becomes eligible
- Create src/vibey_tools/jira as a workspace member: inbound (ticket -> INTAKE project, comment -> human-gate answer, transition -> design accept) and outbound (milestone/status sync), per docs/runbooks/expansion/01-jira-integration.md
- Build the reusable interaction primitive: extract conversation.py's rules (stranger opt-in, self-exclusion, per-thread interaction budget, text-is-data sanitization) into src/vibey_runners/common or a shared tool so every emitting surface inherits them rather than reimplementing
- Create src/vibey/infrastructure/aws/ and gcp/ adapters behind the existing AzureClient-shaped port (src/vibey/application/interfaces/azure.py), generalised so the port is not Azure-named
- Create vibey-social, vibey-career and vibey-word-of-mouth members, each with a responder as well as an emitter, per-repo opt-in and identity labelling
- …and 1 more

### Blockers
- Nothing technical blocks vibey-opencode; the rest of the table is sequenced behind it by the issue itself
- vibey-jira is sequenced behind runbook 12's HTTP/webhook plumbing, which docs/runbooks/expansion/12-integration-surfaces.md:3-9 records as partial (vibey-gh ships the five-surface projection; the conductor has only an outbound WebhookPublisher)

**Notes:** Be careful not to read the opencode failover seat as progress on this issue: it is one string in a default tuple in a machine-level TOML loader for relieving the operator's IDE seat, and it has no connection to the six-phase conductor. Likewise src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/marketplace.py and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json are the Claude Code plugin catalogue (ADR-0034), not family growth.

## Audit status — 2026-09-19

**Status: NOT STARTED · planning size: XL**

Audited against develop/main at `130afa0449fdcc65833f54ede596f0b4e45a145e`. No sibling implementations for jira, social, career, AWS, Azure, GCP, or word-of-mouth are present; the existing OpenCode entry is an engine seat, not this ecosystem. Remaining work is the planned sequence of interactive integrations, provenance, identity, and tests.

The repository gates are green, but this issue remains open because its acceptance scope is not implemented. This comment supersedes older automated status notes assessed against earlier revisions.

## CDD status update — 2026-09-21

**Scope:** the `vibey-opencode` slice of #85 only.
**Status:** **PARTIAL / OPEN** — the parent ecosystem-expansion issue is not closed.

**Evidence cutoff:** local commit `afd31025` on branch `codex/opencode-runner-20260921`; no PR is open.

- Added the `src/vibey_runners/opencode` workspace tenant and `opencodeloop` CLI.
- Added the root `EngineId.OPENCODE`, descriptor, argv/resume mapping, capacity fixtures, event translation, CI matrix, wheel packaging, Docker copy list, Helm enum, and documentation.
- The adapter uses the documented OpenCode JSON run surface, pins the worktree with `--dir`, uses unattended `--auto`, persists append-only JSONL events and `schema_version=1` snapshots, and resumes with an explicit continuation prompt.
- Verification: tenant tests 15 passed with 100% branch coverage; strict mypy, ruff, format, import-linter, Bandit, wheel assembly, and governance corpus checks passed; the root suite passed `2806 passed, 1 xfailed`, with all four root branch-coverage floors at 100%.
- QwenStorm was used as requested. Its first draft diverged into placeholder architecture without valid tests, so CDD rejected that draft; the accepted adapter above is the repaired, fully tested implementation.
- **Remaining evidence gap:** `opencode` is not installed on this host, so `opencodeloop doctor` reports that it was not found on PATH. Live authenticated OpenCode execution, real-binary conformance, provider billing, and publication of this local branch remain unverified.

No closure is claimed for #85. The remaining ecosystem members and the live OpenCode preflight are still open work.

## CDD status update — PR published

The verified OpenCode slice is now published as [PR #314](https://github.com/the-vibey-project/vibey/pull/314) from `codex/opencode-runner-20260921`.

**Status remains: PARTIAL / OPEN.** This PR does not close #85: the wider ecosystem expansion remains, and the external `opencode` binary is not installed on the development host, so live authenticated execution and real-binary conformance remain unverified.
